notes:
TBox revision (migrated 2026-11-11 to the new layout: three propositional queries, three determinate derived queries, no worlds or indeterminate queries). No real exceptions: the HTML standard lists the void elements (area, base, br, col, embed, hr, img, input, link, meta, source, track, wbr) and forbids an end tag on every one; the self-closing slash is not an end tag, and SVG and MathML elements are foreign, not void. The counterfactual (void elements must be closed, as in XHTML-style markup) is plausible and clearly false. The derived queries name made-up elements (, , ) in the prompt (inheritance, 2 hops); the second is an application (what a developer should write). The old validity question about ("is the markup valid?"), which three models answered wrongly before editing, was replaced by the closing-tag question. The negation is asked as "is it true that ... do not need ..." (all four models misread the "is it false that" form). Scope: the rule is the HTML syntax's; in the XML syntax (XHTML)

is well-formed, which is why the prompts say "in HTML". The near query (the hyperlink element, ) differs from the new answer and does not follow from the edit.
